steps.name: Ingest, QC, and log-normalize expression
caveats: The profile explicitly does not state whether Salmon length correction was applied — do not assume integer counts; the integer-fraction check is mandatory before normalization.
counts.csv is 12000 x 121: expect column 1 to be the gene identifier and columns 2-121 the samples; verify the header row matches metadata sample IDs case-sensitively.
Salmon gene-level 'counts' can be TPM or scaledTPM; if values are non-integer, do NOT run them through count-based size-factor normalization.
Single batch — do not apply any batch correction.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-clustering-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 121 columns: 1 gene-ID column + 120 samples, raw Salmon gene-level output) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-clustering-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (120 rows x 2 columns: sample, condition). Organism: Homo sapiens; tissue: whole blood; design: 60 case vs 60 control, unpaired, single batch. Steps: (1) verify the join — counts columns (case-sensitive) must match the 120 metadata rows exactly, with 60 case and 60 control; (2) decide abundance type by measuring the fraction of non-integer matrix values on a random 10,000-value draw — if essentially all integer, treat as raw counts; otherwise treat as TPM (length-corrected); (3) normalize accordingly: raw counts -> edgeR TMM size factors then log2-CPM, or TPM -> log2(TPM+1); (4) if row names are not gene symbols (e.g. Ensembl IDs), map to HGNC symbols using the installed EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 (fall back to the staged UniProt human ID-mapping table, whose Ensembl column is column 19); keep mapped genes with unique symbols, report the mapping rate; (5) filter genes with CPM (or TPM) >= 1 in at least 10% of samples, report gene counts before/after; (6) per-sample QC: total counts/abundance, median expression, distance from the sample centroid after standardization — flag (do not drop) any sample beyond 3x the median distance; (7) z-score each gene across samples to produce the clustering matrix. Single batch: no batch correction anywhere in the plan.
steps.question: What is the clean, log-normalized, HGNC-symbol-indexed expression matrix for the 120 whole-blood samples (60 cases / 60 controls), and are there any sample-level QC outliers that could distort downstream clustering?
constraints: Resolve the abundance type by the integer-fraction check BEFORE choosing any normalization; record the branch taken and the triggering statistic in the output.
Do not remove any of the 120 samples; flag QC outliers with their statistics but keep all 120 in all downstream steps.
If row names are not HGNC symbols, map them and report the mapping success rate; keep only genes with a unique symbol mapping.
Retain genes with CPM or TPM >= 1 in at least 10% of samples; report the number of genes kept.

Save: log-normalized matrix (genes x 120), z-scored standardized matrix (genes x 120), gene-filter list, ID mapping table if used, per-sample QC table, and a PCA plot of the first 2-3 PCs colored by case/control.
Use only locally installed packages; no network access.
steps.description: Prepare the clustering-ready matrix from the Salmon gene-level output and metadata: resolve the abundance type, normalize, map IDs, filter low-expression genes, per-sample QC, PCA.
acceptance_criteria: A 120 x N matrix (N reported, expected in the low thousands) whose sample IDs exactly match the 120 metadata rows, with 60 case / 60 control verified.
Abundance-type branch (integer counts vs TPM) documented with the integer-fraction statistic.
Both the log-normalized and the standardized matrix saved and dimension-checked against metadata.
Per-sample QC table and a PCA plot colored by condition produced; any flagged outliers named with statistics.

plan.title: Whole-blood case/control consensus clustering: subgroups and stability
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 120 whole-blood bulk RNA-seq samples (60 cases vs 60 controls, single batch) with 12,000 Salmon gene-level features (counts.csv, 12000 x 121) and a 120-row condition table (metadata.csv). The question is whether the samples contain stable subgroups beyond the case/control split, how many, and how stable. Because the matrix is tiny (~1.4M cells), all steps are cheap. T1S1 first resolves the one open format question the profile flags — whether the Salmon 'counts' are integer counts or length-corrected TPM — then normalizes (log2-CPM vs log2(TPM+1)), maps identifiers to HGNC symbols, filters, and z-scores genes for clustering. T1S2 runs consensus clustering on all 120 samples (k=2..10, 200 resamples, 80% subsampling), scores stability with C-index/delta-area plus 100-seed k-means ARI and silhouette, and tests every solution against the case/control vector (ARI, NMI, contingency) to see whether the structure IS, refines, or crosses the condition split. T1S3 confirms within-condition substructure with conditional consensus (cases alone, controls alone, k=2..5) and defines each stable subgroup with top discriminating genes (limma). T1S4 characterizes stable subgroups against locally provisioned human gene sets (MSigDB hallmark, human GO, WikiPathways, human-filtered Reactome — all offline) and reports set specificity across subgroups; if no stable subgroups exist, T1S3/T1S4 report that conclusion with the stability evidence rather than forcing a split.
